doc.title: Keter Betts interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 11, 1996

title: Touring Japan and playing in a guitar trio
summary: Brief talk of trips to Japan with Ella and the freedom and sharp keys of a guitar trio.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: That’s great you got to see, you know, a good part of the world.
And you’ve probably been to Japan also?
In fact I was just there, last time I was there was about five years ago I think it was for the Concord Jazz Festival, but I went over there with Ella two times, two, three times.
When you’re working with a guitar trio, that gives you a lot more room to be a like major soloist almost.
It does. And also it gives you a lot of room to learn A E B and D and all of those strings that the guitar players love.
They like the sharps, don’t they.
I guess that like if you look around if you see horn players you know, well I’m going to be doing certain keys.
